No, wandering and physically nonaggressive agitation are not equivalent. 

Wandering refers to aimless or disoriented walking, often seen in patients with dementia or other cognitive impairments. 

Physically nonaggressive agitation, on the other hand, refers to restless or agitated behavior that does not involve physical aggression towards oneself or others, such as pacing, fidgeting, or verbal outbursts. 

While wandering can be a form of agitation, not all physically nonaggressive agitation involves wandering. The two terms describe distinct behaviors and should not be used interchangeably.
